file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Biener - More options more problems Lost in the health insurance maze.pdf

metadata.title: More options, more problems? Lost in the health insurance maze

raw_text.abstract: While the opportunity to choose from a diverse range of options can be advantageous, consumers often struggle to make optimal decisions in the domain of health insurance. In this study, we examine the effects of decision aids on improving choice optimality in a health insurance setting that allows for variations in coverage but is standardized otherwise. We observe widespread adoption of non‐welfare‐maximizing plans and estimate the treatment effects of increasing transparency and restricting choice on choice optimality.
raw_text.keywords_text: health insurance, policy, value of choice

sections.introduction: Consumers often struggle to determine the best option when selecting health insurance plans from a range of choices. The Swiss mandatory health insurance market provides a setting with standardized coverage and variation only in deductible levels.
sections.data: Administrative data from the Swiss Federal Office of Public Health and survey‐based experimental data collected from 540 participants in a behavioral laboratory experiment in Switzerland.
sections.method: Hypothetical‐choice survey experiment varying deductible menu size and information provision formats, combined with expected utility simulations using population health cost distributions.
sections.results: Providing consequence graphs increases the probability of choosing normatively meaningful deductible plans, but does not significantly reduce financial losses from suboptimal choice. Restricting choice to boundary deductibles increases selection of the optimal high deductible but does not materially lower aggregate welfare losses.
sections.conclusion: Information provision and choice restriction improve selection of normatively sensible plans but do not eliminate economically meaningful welfare losses from suboptimal deductible choice.

empirical_analysis.Proxy_for_Y: indicator for selecting CHF 2500 deductible (optimal under expected utility for young adults) and total cost difference between chosen and optimal deductible using Swiss FOPH health cost distributions
empirical_analysis.Proxy_for_X: experimental assignment to consequence graphs, probability information, capped cost display, simplified probabilities, or restricted two‐option menu
empirical_analysis.methodology: hypothetical survey experiment with randomized treatment arms and expected utility simulation benchmarking
empirical_analysis.results: controls for age, gender, expected health costs, math literacy; alternative specification using subjective belief‐based optimality; linear probability and logit models
empirical_analysis.dataset_and_period: Swiss mandatory health insurance context; laboratory and online experiment conducted March 2019 and June 2020 with 540 participants; population health cost data from Swiss FOPH 2017–2019
empirical_analysis.control_variables: age, gender, income category, subjective health, expected annual health costs, risk aversion, math literacy
Topic_L1: Assess whether information provision and choice restriction improve optimal deductible selection in Swiss health insurance.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Boonen - Pareto‐efficient risk sharing in centralized insurance markets with application to.pdf

metadata.title: Pareto‐efficient risk sharing in centralized insurance markets with application to flood risk

raw_text.abstract: This paper provides a microeconomic study of risk‐sharing mechanisms in centralized insurance markets with multiple policyholders and a monopolistic insurer. It characterizes Pareto optimal contracts and applies the framework to flood insurance.
raw_text.keywords_text: risk sharing, flood insurance, Pareto efficiency

sections.introduction: Centralized insurance markets include public programs such as the National Flood Insurance Program. The paper studies optimal risk sharing between multiple policyholders and a centralized insurer.
sections.data: Illustrative empirical application using OpenFEMA flood claims data (1970–2022) aggregated monthly by state.
sections.method: Theoretical characterization of Pareto optimal contracts under coherent risk measures and application to state‐level flood loss data.
sections.results: Risk aggregation and geographic diversification increase maximum welfare gains; correlated risks reduce diversification benefits; risk appetite of one state affects indemnities of others.
sections.conclusion: Centralized multilateral contracting improves welfare relative to bilateral contracts and has implications for public flood insurance design.

theoretical_summary: Characterizes Pareto‐efficient indemnity and premium structures in centralized insurance markets with multiple policyholders and applies the framework to flood risk aggregation.

metadata.title: Loan guarantees and SMEs' investments under asymmetric information and Bayesian learning

raw_text.abstract: We develop a dynamic investment model with loan guarantees wherein insurers face information disadvantages and learn about borrower quality. Borrowers signal their qualities through investment timing, which is characterized by the investment threshold and elapsed time. We derive the conditions for separating or pooling equilibria. We show that the separating investment threshold is constant and determined mainly by the maximum threshold preventing mimicry. If project risk is higher (lower) than the market growth rate, the pooling investment threshold declines (increases) with elapsed time, and learning enhances (reduces) the willingness of high-quality borrowers to wait. Learning alleviates adverse selection and reduces guarantee costs. These effects are more pronounced with a greater uncertainty of the insurer on borrower quality. We reveal dual effects of waiting. The worse the market prospect, the higher the value of waiting in pooling outcomes. Fee-for-guarantee swaps are superior to equity-for-guarantee swaps in environments with marked information asymmetry.
raw_text.keywords_text: asymmetric information; Bayesian learning; loan guarantees; real investment; signaling game

sections.introduction: The paper studies SME investment under loan guarantees with asymmetric information and Bayesian learning about borrower quality.
sections.results: Learning reduces adverse selection and guarantee costs, affects pooling versus separating equilibria, and changes optimal investment thresholds over time.
sections.conclusion: Bayesian learning mitigates adverse selection and improves efficiency of loan guarantee contracts.

theoretical_summary: A dynamic real options signaling model shows how Bayesian learning under loan guarantees shapes separating and pooling equilibria and reduces adverse selection.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Murphy - The risk screening effect of digital insurance distribution.pdf

metadata.title: The risk screening effect of digital insurance distribution

raw_text.abstract: Extant research holds that digital sales channels advance competition and service or goods availability but rarely details the attendant information asymmetry. Leveraging a large unique dataset, this study examines a specific case in which consumers have a choice between offline and digital channels for insurance purchases. We find that digital channels screen in consumers with lower unobserved risk. For term life, endowment and disease insurance products, the average risks of the policies purchased through digital channels were significantly lower than those purchased offline after controlling for all observed risk characteristics. This risk screening effect mainly comes from the inclusion of new low-risk enrollees. As a consequence, digital channels exhibit lower information asymmetry and greater profitability compared to offline channels.
raw_text.keywords_text: digital economy; information asymmetry; insurance distribution; mobile application; risk screening

sections.introduction: The paper studies how digital insurance distribution affects risk selection and information asymmetry.
sections.data: Proprietary data from a large Chinese life insurer on term life, endowment, and disease insurance policies sold via mobile APP and offline channels.
sections.results: Policies purchased via digital channels exhibit significantly lower claim probabilities and loss ratios after controlling for pricing factors and observable characteristics.
sections.conclusion: Digital distribution screens lower unobserved risks and reduces information asymmetry and improves profitability.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Oskam - Supplementing risk adjustment with high‐risk pooling using historical data for.pdf

metadata.title: Supplementing risk adjustment with high-risk pooling using historical data for identifying the high risks

raw_text.abstract: Many regulated health insurance markets with community-rated premiums rely on risk adjustment (RA) to mitigate insurer-incentives to risk select. However, insurers remain typically undercompensated for chronically ill enrollees. We use historical data on health spending and risk adjuster information to identify individuals undercompensated by the Dutch RA model of 2021 and find a selective group (1% of the population) with an average annual undercompensation of €6,050. We supplement the RA model with a risk sharing modality called high-risk pooling (HRP) to organize residual-based compensations towards insurers for the identified group to reduce the mean undercompensation to zero. The effects are evaluated on subgroups defined by chronic disease, finding a 42% reduction of their average undercompensation. Therefore, through compensating 1% of the population, the insurer-incentives to select against chronically ill individuals substantially diminish. These results are compared to outlier-risk sharing (reinsurance), proving HRP to be more effective at reducing selection incentives.
raw_text.keywords_text: health insurance; risk adjustment; risk equalization; risk selection

sections.introduction: The paper evaluates residual undercompensation in the Dutch health insurance risk adjustment model and proposes high-risk pooling.
sections.data: Nationwide Dutch administrative data on health spending, risk adjusters, prior-year spending, and GP diagnostic data.
sections.results: Top 1% predicted residual spenders are undercompensated by about €6,050; high-risk pooling reduces mean undercompensation for chronic disease groups by 42%.
sections.conclusion: High-risk pooling targeted at predicted high-risk individuals effectively reduces selection incentives compared to traditional outlier risk sharing.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Ci - Children as insurance revisited Impact of children on private insurance adoption among.pdf

metadata.title: Children as insurance revisited: Impact of children on private insurance adoption among older parents

raw_text.abstract: The old-age security motive for fertility implies that children are substitutes for parents' old-age insurance. However, demographic dynamics and the evolution of social welfare schemes may challenge this notion. Meanwhile, as population aging is placing heavy pressure on the social security systems, private insurance has become a crucial supplement for hedging risks. In light of the present trends, this research examines the impact of the number of children on private insurance adoption among older parents in China. This research exploits the Later, Longer, Fewer campaign to instrument variations in the number of children. Instrumental variable estimates reveal that the likelihood of older parents having private insurance increases with the number of children they have. The positive effect is more pronounced among older adults, who are less reliant on children and have more access to alternative resources. Further analyses indicate that adverse selection and information channels are potential mechanisms.
raw_text.keywords_text: fertility, number of children, old-age risk, private insurance

sections.data: Uses 2010–2018 Chinese General Social Survey (CGSS) combined with provincial fertility policy timing and historical fertility rates.
sections.method: Constructs policy exposure index based on the Later, Longer, Fewer campaign and estimates causal impact of number of children on private insurance participation.
sections.results: Number of children positively affects private health and pension insurance adoption; effect stronger among self-reliant and resource-rich older adults.
sections.conclusion: Children complement rather than substitute private insurance in modern China; private insurance demand increases with family size due to risk exposure and information channels.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Eastman - Enterprise risk management and corporate tax planning.pdf

metadata.title: Enterprise risk management and corporate tax planning

raw_text.abstract: This study examines the impact of enterprise risk management (ERM) programs on corporate tax planning. ERM is a holistic approach to managing an enterprise's entire portfolio of risks. We hand-collect data on ERM adoption for a sample of Standard & Poor's 500 firms from 1993 to 2016. We empirically document that firms with ERM programs have lower cash effective tax rates than firms without ERM. Additionally, we find that the relation between ERM and tax avoidance is stronger among firms with more business segments. Finally, our results suggest ERM adoption offsets an increase in opacity and tax uncertainty typically associated with tax avoidance strategies. Overall, we provide evidence that ERM allows firms to exploit tax avoidance opportunities through enhanced coordination and communication.
raw_text.keywords_text: enterprise risk management, opacity, tax avoidance, tax uncertainty

sections.data: Hand-collected ERM adoption data for S&P 500 firms 1993–2016 merged with Compustat and related databases.
sections.method: Difference-in-differences framework comparing adopters and nonadopters; cash ETR measures used.
sections.results: ERM adoption lowers cash effective tax rates; effect stronger in firms with more segments; ERM offsets opacity and tax uncertainty increases.
sections.conclusion: ERM facilitates tax avoidance through coordination and communication while reducing associated uncertainty.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Gallenstein - Does inequality impede risk management Evidence from a lab experiment in.pdf

metadata.title: Does inequality impede risk management? Evidence from a lab experiment in Ghana

raw_text.abstract: Low income households in agrarian developing economies face considerable livelihood risks, which have negative impacts on welfare. A growing literature focuses on internal constraints on development, which can negatively affect saving and investment behavior. Here I propose that internal constraints may also hinder risk management. Specifically, I present a theoretical model that explores how fairness preferences may create an internal constraint on risk sharing, particularly in a context of wealth inequality, and thereby also affect demand for formal insurance. To test this theory, I utilize a lab experiment, conducted in Ghana, to investigate the impact of wealth inequality on utilization of risk-management tools, interpersonal risk sharing and formal insurance, and explore how fairness preferences may mediate this effect. I find that inequality reduces risk sharing and increases demand for insurance. Moreover, I find suggestive evidence that fairness preferences create an internal constraint on risk sharing under inequality.
raw_text.keywords_text: fairness, inequality, insurance, lab experiment, risk sharing

sections.method: Experimental design varying initial endowment equality and insurance availability; risk-sharing offers and acceptance observed.
sections.results: Inequality reduces risk-sharing acceptance and increases insurance uptake for high-wealth participants.
sections.conclusion: Fairness preferences under inequality constrain informal risk sharing and raise formal insurance demand.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2024 - Garbarino - The effect of subsidized flood insurance on real estate markets.pdf

metadata.title: The effect of subsidized flood insurance on real estate markets

raw_text.abstract: Subsidized insurance against extreme weather events improves affordability among households in at-risk areas but it can weaken the risk signal via property prices. Leveraging a granular data set of all property transactions and flood events in England, we study the effects of a reinsurance scheme that lowers insurance premiums for at-risk properties. We document that the introduction of this scheme increases prices and transaction volumes of flood-prone properties. This fully offsets the negative direct effects of flooding on property prices, with high-income areas and high-value properties benefiting relatively more. Our findings speak to the debate on climate adaptation policies and their consequences for wealth distribution.
raw_text.keywords_text: climate risks, flood insurance, flood risk, house prices

sections.introduction: Analyzes how UK Flood Re subsidized reinsurance scheme affects property prices and liquidity in flood-prone areas.
sections.data: Universe of property transactions in England 1995–2020 matched with flood maps and flood event data.
sections.method: Difference-in-differences comparing flood-prone and non-prone properties before and after Flood Re introduction in 2016.
sections.results: Flood Re offsets flood-related price discounts and increases transaction probabilities, with stronger effects in high-income areas.
sections.conclusion: Subsidized flood insurance raises property values in at-risk areas and has distributional implications.

file.path: /mnt/data/J of Risk Insurance - 2025 - Ellis - Registered index‐linked annuities in qualified retirement plans.pdf

metadata.title: Registered index-linked annuities in qualified retirement plans

raw_text.abstract: Many Americans remain financially underprepared for retirement. While automatic enrollment in employer-sponsored retirement plans has helped, target-date funds (TDFs) used as default investments have limitations. We propose target-date registered index-linked annuities (TD-RILAs) as a transparent, cost-effective alternative providing decreasing equity exposure over time. A theoretical analysis explores TD-RILAs' optimal structure and compares them to TDFs. A lab experiment examines investors' preferences, product transparency, default choices, and the role of information. We find that TD-RILAs are a suitable addition to retirement plans, potentially rivaling TDFs.
raw_text.keywords_text: registered index-linked annuities, retirement, target date fund
